06ae5df0f9.q: What is TechCentro and what makes it unique as a workforce development program?
06ae5df0f9.a: TechCentro is a bilingual workforce development center offering adult basic education, employment services, and occupational training in allied health and skilled trades. It provides English language support, partnerships with community organizations to address barriers like transportation and childcare, and focuses on workplace English rather than conversational English, helping trainees advance to supervisory positions through improved communication skills.
06ae5df0f9.e: Building Futures: Tec Centro's Workforce Impact with Robert Torres

4227cd5126.q: How many TechCentro locations exist and where is the Harrisburg center modeled from?
4227cd5126.a: There are six TechCentro locations total. The Harrisburg center is modeled after Lancaster's centers, which have been operating for more than 10 years and were so successful that Reading, Lebanon, York, and Harrisburg each opened their own centers following the same model.
4227cd5126.e: Building Futures: Tec Centro's Workforce Impact with Robert Torres

7e3f086892.q: What specific trade programs does TechCentro offer or plan to offer?
7e3f086892.a: TechCentro offers and plans to offer facilities maintenance, plumbing, HVAC, refrigeration, electromechanical, welding, and renewable energy solar training. The Harrisburg center is kicking off with facilities maintenance in a couple of weeks in partnership with Harrisburg Area Community College, and is still recruiting instructors for plumbing, HVAC, and other trades.
7e3f086892.e: Building Futures: Tec Centro's Workforce Impact with Robert Torres

e172bf74a4.q: What are the main challenges TechCentro faces in launching its construction trades programs?
e172bf74a4.a: The primary challenge has been recruiting instructors, particularly qualified people willing to teach part-time or full-time. Robert Torres is reconsidering whether to offer full-time positions if instructors can teach multiple classes, and emphasizes the need for instructors who can evaluate adults, recognize weaknesses, and teach critical problem-solving skills, even if they lack prior teaching experience.
e172bf74a4.e: Building Futures: Tec Centro's Workforce Impact with Robert Torres

d2465134b2.q: Who is eligible to enroll in TechCentro's skilled trades programs?
d2465134b2.a: The programs are intended for adults who have graduated from high school. While high school students who have graduated and want to explore trades are welcome, TechCentro is not working with anyone who has not yet graduated. The center prioritizes adults in areas with high poverty rates like Harrisburg, where the poverty rate is much higher than the state average.
d2465134b2.e: Building Futures: Tec Centro's Workforce Impact with Robert Torres

7951eec97f.q: What is the application and vetting process for TechCentro students?
7951eec97f.a: Prospective students fill out an interest form on the website (techcentralcr.org), then TechCentro conducts interviews to assess commitment to the program schedule. For health programs, immunizations, TB tests, and criminal background checks are required. The center also plans to administer basic 15 to 30 minute reading and math assessments to identify areas of concern before training begins.
7951eec97f.e: Building Futures: Tec Centro's Workforce Impact with Robert Torres

1ee868c5ba.q: How does TechCentro partner with employers to improve training outcomes?
1ee868c5ba.a: TechCentro invites employers to conduct mock interviews, give presentations on soft skills, and hold lunch and learn sessions. UPMC and Penn State Health have participated in the healthcare side, emphasizing that technical skills are assumed after certification; employers prioritize soft skills like teamwork and communication. Torres plans to model the same employer partnership approach with construction trades, building a network to provide feedback on curriculum and placement opportunities.
1ee868c5ba.e: Building Futures: Tec Centro's Workforce Impact with Robert Torres

3fa8279d48.q: What is the typical class size and what additional programs does TechCentro plan to offer?
3fa8279d48.a: The average class size is about 10 students per session. Torres plans to expand into welding and offer standalone courses in construction basics, safety, OSHA 10, math, and blueprint reading to build a waitlist for full programs like plumbing, HVAC, welding, and electromechanical, allowing the center to maintain continuous engagement and capacity.

c7e8653468.q: What makes starting a construction management program from scratch so difficult for an academic institution?
c7e8653468.a: Creating a program requires understanding the curriculum developed by other faculty, understanding what each course teaches and how they build on each other, ensuring courses integrate with safety programs offering OSHA 40 certification, civil engineering courses, and business courses. The hardest part is keeping students current with real-time industry changes and technology so they are fully prepared and a real asset when they graduate.

c02061cbf2.q: How does a construction management program balance multiple specializations and career paths?
c02061cbf2.a: The Slippery Rock program has zero specialization, allowing students to explore different areas including highway construction, building, and residential work. The advisory board was shaped partly by student input on their career visions. Students are exposed to various roles through job site tours and guest speakers including owners, project managers, specialty contractors, and executives like the senior vice president for construction at UPMC.
c02061cbf2.e: Thinking About a Career in Construction? Inside Slippery Rock University's New Construction Management Program with Amanda McIsaac

dcdd5a6ba2.q: What is the most critical gap identified by construction industry professionals in new graduates entering the field?
dcdd5a6ba2.a: According to feedback from the first board meeting in March, communication was identified almost unanimously as a major gap. Industry professionals noted that new graduates often rely on abbreviated text messages and ChatGPT-generated emails, but construction is relationship-based and requires effective communication with subs, material suppliers, and field teams.
dcdd5a6ba2.e: Thinking About a Career in Construction? Inside Slippery Rock University's New Construction Management Program with Amanda McIsaac

9bd302496f.q: How does integrating OSHA 40-hour certification into the junior year benefit construction management students?
9bd302496f.a: Students earn their 40-hour OSHA certification during their junior year, allowing them to go directly onto job sites with boots on the ground on day one of internships. This also enables the class to visit active project sites and understand jobsite safety protocols as visitors and guests, which is important for preventing accidents due to distraction or awe when observing construction activities.
9bd302496f.e: Thinking About a Career in Construction? Inside Slippery Rock University's New Construction Management Program with Amanda McIsaac

d4d3a05345.q: What unique advantages does a career in construction management offer compared to other engineering disciplines?
d4d3a05345.a: With construction, students have the opportunity with their hands to build something and see progress almost daily, from nothing to a finished product. Unlike some other engineering paths, construction offers constant variety—after finishing one project that may last one or two years, students move to a new job and new project, constantly making and bettering communities and environments.
d4d3a05345.e: Thinking About a Career in Construction? Inside Slippery Rock University's New Construction Management Program with Amanda McIsaac

9a395cecf1.q: How is Slippery Rock University integrating real campus projects into the construction management curriculum?
9a395cecf1.a: The program works closely with Juan Perez, head of facilities, on actual university projects. Freshmen put together a proposal for work at Storm Harbor equestrian facility, and junior-seniors did similar work on Morrow Fieldhouse. Students receive actual blueprints, attend site walks, ask questions, and see how amendments are submitted and bids are calculated—giving them experience with real projects being bid by the university.

36625f02c9.q: What role does mentorship play in shaping construction management careers according to industry experience?
36625f02c9.a: Amanda McIsaac credits her long-term mentor for her career development over 15 years, noting he pushed her out of her comfort zone while fully supporting her and allowing her to learn from mistakes. She believes mentorship is overlooked and plans to have her mentor call in to meet her sophomores, as it is valuable regardless of career field and especially important for newer graduates unless their company has a formal program.
